card.name: Last word before a sentence-ending period
card.fires_on: The final word of a sentence in news or essay prose, just before the period, often a short punchy closer such as off, much, profound, wrong or too.

modes.label: Closing adverb or particle
modes.description: A short particle or adverb completes a verb phrase right before the period.
modes.example: the effort is finally paying<< off>>. Over the past decade, deCODE

modes.label: Closing adjective or noun
modes.description: An adjective or noun ends a sentence as a flat statement, not an exclamation.
modes.example: could be<< profound>>. Like Marie Curie over a century

card.writes: It favors a sentence ending in a period and suppresses exclamation marks, so the sentence closes calmly.
card.plain: It fires on the last word of a plain sentence, when the next mark should be a period, not an exclamation point.
